messages:
incident-bot: Paging eng-oncall: High error rate on /v1/rerank-batch in prod (us-west-2). Route: embeddings -> reranker. Error class: downstream shape mismatch. Severity: P2. Please ack. :rotating_light:

alex: Acked. I'm oncall for eng-sre. Starting triage. What are initial signals?

maria: noticed spikes ~1937654200, rerank 500s and 502s. Grafana: request_error_rate -> 4.2% from baseline 0.1%.

jon: throwing this in thread — stack traces from edge: `ValueError: expected input with shape (N,768) got (N,770)` coming from reranker_forward -> linear.py

kevin: copying relevant logs from batch endpoint (masked service keys):
```
2026-03-15T14:12:43Z batch-worker-12 ERROR payload_validation failed: vector_len=770 expected=768 request_id=req_0a9f
2026-03-15T14:12:44Z batch-router-3 WARN dropping request req_0a9f after 2 retries
2026-03-15T14:12:45Z reranker-87 ERROR forward failed: ValueError: matmul shapes not aligned
```

emma: customer-impact quick note: internal telemetry shows ~12 customers observed elevated rerank latencies/errors (mostly interactive search and snippet rerank). No large contracts paging yet but one demo customer reported flakiness.

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause batching at batch endpoint for the canary model (adds latency but avoids shape mismatch), 2) route traffic away from newly onboarded embedding model variant, 3) add adapter to pad/truncate vectors at reranker input as a stopgap. Thoughts?

maria: we rolled a new embedding variant last night (quantized-embed-v2) for canary traffic ~1937652000. Hypothesis A: quantized variant produces slightly different vector length due to post-processing bug. Hypothesis B: request marshaling at batch endpoint adding metadata to vector buffer.

jon: confirming: the batch endpoint expects serialized vectors as length 768 floats. I see in the serialization code we recently added a 2-byte checksum header in front of each vector for v2 — that could cause deserialization to read wrong stride if not handled. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/embeds/PR/4521 (added checksum)

kevin: I can push a quick fix to the batch deserializer to skip checksum if present, but that risks affecting other clients. Safer to disable checksum-on-write in canary for now.

emma: mitigation path chosen: 1) pause batching on rerank-batch workers serving canary (will route single-request processing), 2) rollback checksum write in canary embedding producer, 3) enable input-shape guard in reranker that returns 400 with clear error for malformed vectors rather than 500.

alex: I'm initiating step 1 now — disabling batching policy for pool `embed-rerank-canary` (command run):
```
$ redwoodctl pool update embed-rerank-canary --batching disabled --dry-run=false
Applied change to pool embed-rerank-canary
```

jon: I see reduced 500s from 4.2% -> 1.1% within 30s. Good signal.

maria: starting rollback of checksum write in canary producer (deploy in progress). Noting deploy id: deploy_20260315_0932.

kevin: patch to deserializer prepared as backup:
```
# src/deserialize.py
if len(payload) == expected_len + 2 and payload[:2] == CHECKSUM_MAGIC:
    payload = payload[2:]
```
Will keep ready but not deploy unless rollback fails.

emma: customer-impact update: error rate continues trending down. I'll message CS to prep a short blurb for affected customers: minimal impact, temporary mitigation, full RCA to follow.

maria: deploy rollback finished at ~1937654380. Monitoring logs...

jon: post-rollback logs show normalized vector_len=768 and no further matmul errors in reranker. Example: `2026-03-15T14:13:24Z batch-worker-15 INFO deserialized vector_len=768 request_id=req_0b2a`

alex: closing mitigation: re-enable batching after 2 minutes of stable metrics? Or keep disabled until we confirm end-to-end? Pros/cons?

kevin: batching gives 3-4x cost savings; re-enable only after full e2e canary run and a unit test added for checksum header handling. I'll add tests and a canary job. ETA 2h.

maria: adding to hypothesis tracker in-thread: A) checksum header introduced mismatch on v2 embed producer (supported by PR and logs) B) batch router did not validate vector length before grouping (observed) C) reranker should be resilient and validate input shapes (observed 500s).

jon: action items assigned inline: alex -> coordinate customer comms and finalize mitigation plan; kevin -> unit tests + optional patch for deserializer (PR ready); maria -> write timeline + link logs; emma -> notify CS and monitor; jon -> create retro ticket and collect stack traces.

alex: quick timeline (to paste into RCA doc):
- 1937652000: canary quantized-embed-v2 released (~10% traffic)
- 1937654200: first errors spike observed on rerank-batch
- 1937654250: incident-bot paged eng-oncall
- 1937654270: batching disabled on embed-rerank-canary pool (mitigation start)
- 1937654380: canary rollback completed (checksum write reverted)
- 1937654400: error rate back to baseline

maria: I'll collect and zip logs for RCA and attach to ticket: https://tickets.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0315-embed-rerank. Will include sample request_ids: req_0a9f, req_0b2a, req_0c33.

kevin: follow-up: adding end-to-end test in CI that serializes embedding vectors with/without checksum and ensures batch deserializer handles both. I'll open PR after unit tests.

emma: note for postmortem: estimate customer-impact window ~5-8 minutes for most customers; one demo experienced repeated failures during demo (CS notified).

alex: excellent. I'll mark this thread as mitigation successful and move to RCA-writing. If anyone sees another spike, ping oncall. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315 created and assigned to eng-sre. Timeline and logs archived at https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0315/archive

alex: thanks all, closing here and starting formal RCA doc.
